prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2015 manifesto centres on leaving the EU to restore UK sovereignty, control immigration, refocus public spending on domestic priorities, and overhaul politics to give voters more direct power.

Fiscal stance and tax: UKIP claims its plans are independently costed (Cebr). Savings come from leaving the EU (c. £9bn/yr), cutting overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, replacing the Barnett formula, and reducing government/quango costs. These fund: an extra £12bn for the NHS over five years; £5.2bn more for social care; £1.5bn for mental health/dementia; +6,000 frontline police/prison/border posts; defence spending at/above 2% of GDP; free hospital parking; carers +£572/yr; STEMM/medicine tuition-fee waivers tied to UK work; brownfield housing incentives. Tax cuts include raising the personal allowance to at least £13,000, a new 30% band between £43.5k–£55k, lifting the 40% threshold to £55k, abolishing inheritance tax, ending income tax on the minimum wage, increasing the transferable allowance for married couples/civil partners, and zero-rating VAT on listed-building repairs and sanitary products.

Immigration: Leave the EU to end free movement; introduce an Australian-style, non-discriminatory points system; five‑year moratorium on unskilled immigration; cap high‑skill work visas at 50,000 p.a.; five‑year qualification for benefits and most NHS access; more Border Agency staff and exit/entry tracking; tougher action on illegal immigration, sham marriages, and foreign criminals; no amnesty.

NHS and social care: Protect a free-at-point-of-use NHS; hire 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP pilots in A&E; boost mental health and dementia services; scrap PFI use; create manager licensing; replace CQC/Monitor with local professional health boards; tackle “health tourism.”

Welfare, disability, pensions: Scrap the bedroom tax; retain under‑25s’ housing benefit; GP/specialist‑led capability assessments; raise Carer’s Allowance; support foodbanks with advisers. Flexible state pension “window” to allow earlier, actuarially reduced take-up; stronger anti‑scam rules; war widows’ pensions for life.

Education and childcare: Expand school diversity, including more grammar and vocational/technical options; abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; streamline Ofsted; STEMM/medicine fee waivers; age-appropriate sex education at secondary only. Deregulate childcare vouchers to widen provision; require wrap‑around care (8am–6pm) in primaries.

Housing and environment: Prioritise brownfield (register, grants, stamp duty relief); bring empty homes into use; restrict social housing to those with five years’ tax/NI; homelessness register; protect green belt; local referenda on large developments.

Transport and energy: Scrap HS2; targeted speed cameras only; oppose road pricing; remove tolls; scrap HGV DCPC; double foreign HGV levy. Repeal the Climate Change Act; end new wind/solar subsidies; back shale gas with safeguards; support coal/nuclear/hydro; cut green levies from bills.

Jobs and small business: Enforce minimum wage; curb EU jobs portal/relocation grants; code to curb zero‑hours abuse; cut small business rates (20% relief up to £50k rateable value); penalise serial late payers; improve SME access to public contracts.

Rural, farming, animal welfare, fishing: New, capped Single Farm Payment focused on smaller/family farms; support dairy co‑ops; stronger cruelty penalties; CCTV in abattoirs; ban live exports for slaughter. Leave the CFP; regain a 200‑mile EEZ; boost under‑10m boats; end destructive practices.

Crime, justice, political reform, local government, culture: More frontline policing; deport foreign criminals; UK Bill of Rights, leave ECHR; curb EU justice measures like the EAW; tough on trafficking, FGM, forced marriage; decriminalise TV licence non‑payment. Political reforms include citizens’ initiatives, real recall, confirmation/expenditure hearings, and proportional voting. Local referenda on major planning; weekly bins where desired. Promote British values, English as the default official language (with Welsh/Gaelic as appropriate); new bank holidays for St George’s and St David’s.

Trade, defence, aid, Brexit: Regain WTO seat and strike UK trade deals post‑Brexit; maintain cooperation with Europe on shared interests. Rebuild armed forces, retain Trident, oppose an EU army, tax relief for deployed personnel. Cut aid to 0.2% GNI, focus on emergency relief, WASH, vaccinations; merge DFID into the FCO. Hold an in/out EU referendum and, on a Leave vote, exit via Article 50 with a UK‑EU trade deal as the goal.
